subject: Renewal proposal: term amendment, consumption kicker & SLA buffer
summary: Customer asked for a temporary price hold and additional committed-discount tied to a consumption kicker. Sales proposed a compromise: limited price hold (90 days), a consumption kicker that returns additional credits if months exceed threshold, and a small SLA buffer during peak season. Finance/Legal looped in for approval; final proposal sent with updated terms and attachments.
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@skyframe.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal: term amendment, consumption kicker & SLA buffer

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our call I attached an updated term sheet that:
- Holds current per-token pricing for the first 90 days post-renewal (to give Skyframe room to ramp).
- Adds a consumption kicker: if monthly usage exceeds the committed tier by >20% for two consecutive months, we apply an incremental credit tranche to offset overage in the following month.
- Includes a small SLA buffer (5% extra capacity headroom) for Nov–Jan to support your holiday traffic.

High-level numbers are on page 2; the term sheet also outlines billing cadence and true‑up mechanics.

Next steps: let me know if Procurement wants us to tighten the price-hold window or change the kickers. If this looks close we can push to signature and schedule the migration window.

Attachments: Skyframe_Renewal_Termsheet_v3.pdf, SLA-buffer-matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@skyframe.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@skyframe.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal: term amendment, consumption kicker & SLA buffer

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turn. Procurement will push back on the 90-day price-hold; they want a 180-day lock and a lower overage exposure (they prefer a fixed discount rather than credits). Two points from my side:

1) If we lock pricing for 180 days, we need a stronger consumption guarantee — can you commit to a max 10% step-up fee after threshold instead of credits?
2) Holiday season is high risk; the SLA buffer looks good but we need explicit response-time targets in the SLA matrix (not just capacity headroom).

I looped Procurement; they may redline the term sheet and return a mark-up.

—Daniel
Head of Platform Engineering, Skyframe
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Skyframe request — 180-day hold / fixed discount ask (need approval)

Marissa / Monica —

FYI: Skyframe is pushing for a 180-day price hold and wants a fixed overage discount instead of our proposed credits. They also want RTT targets added to the SLA matrix for Nov–Jan.

My suggested concession:
- Offer 120-day price hold (compromise).
- Replace pure credits with a consumption kicker that does two things:
  * Months 1–2 overage >20% -> 50% of the overage is credited back the following invoice.
  * Sustained overage (3+ months) -> escalates to a one-time invoice credit equal to 20% of the overage months combined, capped at $75k.
- Update SLA-buffer-matrix.xlsx to include 95th/99th percentile response-time targets during the buffer window (we already have capacity plan).

Asking for quick approval from Sales Ops / Finance on the caps and from Legal on wording for the escalator. If we can accept this, we keep predictable economics and limit downside.

Thoughts? I think 120 days + the two-tier kicker keeps procurement comfortable while protecting unit economics.

Karthik
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Skyframe request — 180-day hold / fixed discount ask (need approval)

Karthik / Marissa —

Finance reviewed. Approve the compromise with these edits:
- Price hold: 120 days (no change).
- Consumption kicker: keep two-tier structure but reduce capped credit from $75k to $50k for this account (Skyframe is mid-market; exposure tolerance is lower).
- SLA: add the 95th/99th p95/p99 RTT targets to SLA-buffer-matrix.xlsx; Legal will add a carve-out that the buffer is operational (not a contractual uptime change).

Legal will push minor language on the escalator clause; I can coordinate and produce a redline for signature. Karthik — please send an updated term sheet with the $50k cap and updated SLA sheet. Once Skyframe signs we can lock start date and billing.

Monica Patel
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
